newsitem.title: USA: US industry praises Japan construction commitments.
newsitem.headline: US industry praises Japan construction commitments.

text.p: The American Forest and Paper Association asked the U.S. Trade Representative Wednesday to take Japan off its Super 301 watch list for wood products, saying Japan had made several market-opening commitments.
In a statement released in Washington, AFPA said it made the request in a letter to Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky.

Promising moves by the Japanese government include the approval of three-storey wooden structures in suburban areas, recognition of U.S. wood grading systems and a commitment to revise Japan's building standards towards one based on performance, the statement said.
Full implementation of Japan's commitments would lead to a 20-percent increase in U.S. sales to Japan, it said. Exports of wood building products to Japan totaled $1 billion last year.

"As a result, we face the exciting prospect of new and expanding growth in our most important offshore market for U.S. building products," the statement quoted Plum Creek Timber Co. President Rick Holley as saying.
Holley was to make the remarks in a speech in Seattle Friday to the National Conference on Housing Export Opportunities to Japan, it said.
Despite the positive developments, the industry would continue to monitor their implementation, including the elimination of tariffs on value-added wood products, the statement said.
